newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel ready to cede most of Hebron to PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel ready to cede most of Hebron to PLO.

text.p: Israeli soldiers opened the gates of their main base to Palestinian police and prepared to leave Hebron after parliament overwhelmingly approved an accord transferring most of the West Bank city to the PLO.
Crowds waving Palestinian flags gathered outside the imposing hilltop headquarters from where Israel has ruled Hebron for 30 years in anticipation of a pullout on Thursday night.
But PLO security chief Jibril Rajoub said Israel would begin its redeployment from 80 percent of the city on Friday morning.
The crowds, drenched by icy rain, drifted away.

"The redeployment will begin at 8 o'clock (0600 GMT) and also the celebrations," Rajoub told reporters after emerging from a brief visit to the Israeli headquarters, which had been stripped of nearly all equipment on Thursday by soldiers who dismantled checkposts throughout the city.
"All the arrangements are ready for the redeployment," Rajoub said.

In Jerusalem, Israel's parliament paved the way for the pullback by endorsing the U.S.-brokered agreement sealed on Thursday by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
The 120-member house voted 87-17, with one abstention, to approve the Hebron deal and three further troop redeployments from mainly rural areas of the West Bank.
The accord, clinched after months of acrimonious negotiations, marked the first time a right-wing government had agreed to hand over territory Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East war to PLO rule.
The main opposition Labour party and left-wing and Arab factions joined with most members of the ruling Likud coalition to ratify the accord after a 12-hour debate.

"I thank the members of the house. I hope in the future, during this government's term, to bring complete peace agreements with the Palestinians and perhaps with Arab nations, in addition to the ones we have signed," Netanyahu told parliament.

Israeli officials said the redeployment would be swift since most equipment had already been dismantled. Israel poured troop and police reinforcments into the town to prevent protests by Jewish settlers opposed to the handover.

An Israeli general issued orders on Thursday restricting the movements of 18 alleged Jewish militants for up to 10 days. Some came from Hebron where 400 settlers live in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs. This makes Hebron unique among the seven West Bank towns already handed over to PLO rule.
Five soldiers for each settler will remain to guard the Jews in the fifth of the town that will remain under Israeli control.
"We are not leaving Hebron, we are redeploying in Hebron," Netanyahu said.
His remarks were aimed at right-wingers and settlers who staged a cabinet revolt against the withdrawal.
Netanyahu muscled the accord through cabinet by an 11-7 majority after a stormy 12-hour meeting that ended on Thursday morning. Science Minister Binyamin Begin resigned in protest.
The prime minister held a televised prime-time news conference on Thursday evening to defend the deal.
He said the Hebron pullback commitment had been "inherited" from the previous Labour-led administration.
"I want to tell you what is not our way: we were not elected to retreat to the (pre-) 1967 (Middle East war) lines and establish a Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital," Netanyahu said.

Palestinian officials said 400 civilian and paramilitary police were poised to take over in Hebron. PLO sources said busloads of Palestinian police had left self-ruled Jericho to overnight in Bethlehem en route to Hebron.
